newsitem.title: FRANCE: "Lebanon is not a free country" - Patriarch Sfeir.
newsitem.headline: "Lebanon is not a free country" - Patriarch Sfeir.

text.p: Lebanese Christian Maronite Patriarch Cardinal Nasrallah Sfeir, speaking before the arrival of Pope John Paul on a historic first visit to Lebanon, was quoted on Friday as saying his was not a free country.

"...elections were organised under Syrian control and... Christians feel they are not represented in government or parliament....Lebanon is not a free country," he said in an interview published by the French daily Le Monde.
"It has neither sovereignty nor independence. Part of its people have been shunted aside," he said.

The Church, led by Sfeir, has become the main postwar spokesman for the bitterness many Christians and some Moslems feel at the presence of 35,000 Syrian troops and the authorities' perceived surrender of decision-making powers to Syria.

Pope John Paul's visit, starting on Saturday and his first to the Middle East in his much-travelled papacy, aims at helping Lebanon's divided Christians find a role in the postwar life of a country created for them by former colonial power France out of the crumbling Ottoman empire.
Sfeir said it was wrong to believe the visit would either put a stamp of approval "on the (Syrian) occupation of our country...or, on the contrary, allow a radical change."

"The Pope is not coming to Lebanon to delve into politics but to recall a number of values which the Christians are very attached to: the right to self-determination, the right of the country to independence and sovereignty, the right of equality for all before the law and respect for justice," he said.
Sfeir said he hoped the visit would help preserve peaceful ties between Christians and Moslems and Lebanon's role as a link between East and West and Islam and Christianity.

Lebanon's Christian minority emerged defeated and divided from the 1975-90 civil war and has largely refused to reconcile itself to the Syrian-dominated government, which many see as undermining their country's independence.
